e-4725.knowledge_point: Transforming a 2x2 Matrix Into the Identity Matrix Using Row Operations
e-4725.problem:
Which of the following matrices are transformed into the $2\times 2$ identity matrix after applying the row operations $R_1 \leftrightarrow R_2 \,$ and $\, R_2 :=  R_2+(-1)R_1?$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14042225/assets/e607bba88cc1f15abaa45fc3cf02110243433d60259c56805515ced373054ca0.png)
e-4725.worked_solution:
Let's apply the operations to each of the matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -3 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times  \\ B & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =I\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$B$ only".

e-4724.knowledge_point: Identifying the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix Calculated Using Row Operations
e-4724.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine $A^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
e-4724.worked_solution:
We write down $A$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $A$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix $A^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14042225/assets/247c0a29294e61735b969d769d8ba3794c0b5e816c3968a8db087740eeb925d8.png)

e-4723.knowledge_point: Determining the Row Operations Required To Find the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix
e-4723.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $A$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to each step?

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2} & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
e-4723.worked_solution:
We write down $A$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $A$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-3){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2} & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
R_1 := \dfrac{1}{2}R_1,
\qquad
R_1 := R_1+(-3)R_2.
$$

The matrix $A^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore,

Let's apply the operations to each of the matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ \frac{1}{4} & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4} & 0 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times  \\ B & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ \frac{1}{4} & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4} & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =I\,✓ \\ C & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ \frac{3}{4} & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4} & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -5 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$B$ only".

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Which of the following matrices are transformed into the $2\times 2$ identity matrix after applying the row operations ${R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1}\,$ and $\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1}?$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}8 & 0 \\ -6 & 1\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ -4 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
after.worked_solution:
Let's apply the operations to each of the matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =I\,✓ \\ B & =[\begin{aligned}8 & 0 \\ -6 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ -6 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times  \\ C & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ -4 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -4 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$A$ only".

after.problem:
Which of the following matrices are transformed into the $2\times 2$ identity matrix after applying the row operations ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}\,$ and $\,{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1}?$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$
after.worked_solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times  \\ B & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =I\,✓ \\ C & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$B$ only".

content.knowledge_point: Transforming a 2x2 Matrix Into the Identity Matrix Using Row Operations
content.problem:
Which of the following matrices are transformed into the $2\times 2$ identity matrix after applying the row operations ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2},\,$ ${R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1},\,$ and $\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1}?$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$
content.worked_solution:
Let's apply the operations to each of the matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =I\,✓ \\ B & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -4 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times  \\ C & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$A$ only".

decision.explanation: Use R1 := R1 − 3R2. The first row becomes [1,0 | −5,−3], while the second remains [0,1 | 2,1]. Thus the right-hand block is A⁻¹ = [[−5,−3],[2,1]].

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine ${A}^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & -5 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
We write down $A$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $A$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & -5 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-3){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -5 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix ${A}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{A}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}-5 & -3 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

decision.explanation: Complete the process with R2 := (1/5)R2. The second row becomes [0,1 | −3/5,1/5], while the first remains [1,0 | 1,0]. Thus B⁻¹ = [[1,0],[−3/5,1/5]].

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $B$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine ${B}^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[B\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 5 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
We write down $B$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $B$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[B\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 5 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{3}{5} & \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix ${B}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{B}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -\frac{3}{5} & \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 7
?

The inverse of the 2×2 matrix B is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine B−1.

[B|I]=[10103501]R2:=R2+(−3)R1∼[101005−31]R2:=___________∼[10aa01aa]

a
B−1=[1035−15]
b
B−1=[10−3515]
c
B−1=[1−135−15]
d
 B−1=[103515]
e
B−1=[13−3515]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We write down B and the identity matrix I side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix B into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

[B|I]=[10103501]R2:=R2+(−3)R1∼[101005−31]R2:=15R2∼[101001−3515]

The matrix B−1 is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore,

B−1=[10−3515].

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix Calculated Using Row Operations
content.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $B$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine ${B}^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[B\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 5 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
We write down $B$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $B$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[B\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 5 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{3}{5} & \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix ${B}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{B}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -\frac{3}{5} & \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}].
$$

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $D$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine ${D}^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[D\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
We write down $D$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $D$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[D\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix ${D}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{D}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix Calculated Using Row Operations
content.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $D$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine ${D}^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[D\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
We write down $D$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $D$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[D\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix ${D}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{D}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 9

The inverse of the 2×2 matrix C is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine C−1.

[C|I]=[171021501]R2:=R2+(−2)R1∼[171001−21]R1:=___________∼[10aa01aa]

a
C−1=[17−21]
b

C−1=[15−271]

C−1=[15−7−21]

decision.explanation: Use R1 := R1 − 7R2. The first row becomes [1,0 | 15,−7], and the second remains [0,1 | −2,1]. Thus C⁻¹ = [[15,−7],[−2,1]].

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $C$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine ${C}^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[C\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 15 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
We write down $C$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $C$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[C\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 15 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-7){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 15 & -7 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix ${C}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{C}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}15 & -7 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 9

The inverse of the 2×2 matrix C is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine C−1.

[C|I]=[171021501]R2:=R2+(−2)R1∼[171001−21]R1:=___________∼[10aa01aa]

a
C−1=[17−21]
b
C−1=[−21157]
c
C−1=[15−271]
d
C−1=[5721]
e
C−1=[15−7−21]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We write down C and the identity matrix I side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix C into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

[C|I]=[171021501]R2:=R2+(−2)R1∼[171001−21]R1:=R1+(−7)R2∼[1015−701−21]

The matrix C−1 is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, C−1=[15−7−21].

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix Calculated Using Row Operations
content.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $C$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine ${C}^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[C\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 15 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
We write down $C$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $C$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[C\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 15 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-7){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 15 & -7 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix ${C}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{C}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}15 & -7 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

after.name: Question 10
after.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine ${A}^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 5 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
We write down $A$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $A$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 5 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{2}{5} & \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix ${A}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{A}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -\frac{2}{5} & \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}].
$$

The matrix ${A}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{A}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -\frac{2}{5} & \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}].
$$

a
R1:=R1+2R2,R2:=R2−R1
b
R1:=R1−R2,R2:=R2+2R1

R1:=R1−R2,R2:=R2+3R1

decision.explanation: First, R1 + R2 = [1,0,1,1]. Then, using the updated first row, R2 + 3R1 = [0,1,3,4]. These are exactly the displayed steps.

after.name: Question 11
after.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $Y$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to each step?

$$
\begin{aligned}[Y\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ -3 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
We write down $Y$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $Y$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[Y\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ -3 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+{R}_{2},\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1}.
$$

The matrix ${Y}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{Y}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

after.html:
Question 11
?

The inverse of the matrix Y is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to each step?

[Y|I]=[4−110−3101]___________∼[1011−3101]___________∼[10110134]

a
R1:=R1+2R2,R2:=R2−R1
b
R1:=R1−R2,R2:=R2+2R1
c
R1:=R1−R2,R2:=R2+3R1
d
R1:=R1+3R2,R2:=R2−2R1
e
R1:=R1+R2,R2:=R2+3R1
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We write down Y and the identity matrix I side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix Y into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

[Y|I]=[4−110−3101]R1:=R1+R2∼[1011−3101]R2:=R2+3R1∼[10110134]

The corresponding row operations are R1:=R1+R2,R2:=R2+3R1.

The matrix Y−1 is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore,

Y−1=[1134].

verification.explanation: Rechecking confirms R1 := R1 + R2 produces [1,0,1,1]. Then R2 := R2 + 3R1 produces [0,1,3,4], using the updated first row. This agrees with the worked solution.

content.knowledge_point: Determining the Row Operations Required To Find the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix
content.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $Y$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to each step?

$$
\begin{aligned}[Y\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ -3 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
We write down $Y$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $Y$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[Y\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ -3 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+{R}_{2},\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1}.
$$

The matrix ${Y}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{Y}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 12
?

The inverse of the matrix U is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to each step?

[U|I]=[11102301]___________∼[111001−21]___________∼[103−101−21]

a
R2:=R2+(−1)R1,R1:=R1+(−2)R2
b
R2:=R2+2R1,R1:=R1+R2
c
R2:=R2+(−2)R1,R1:=R1+R2
d
R2:=R2+(−2)R1,R1:=R1+(−1)R2
e
R2:=R2+(−3)R1,R1:=R1+(−2)R2
Submit

decision.explanation: First, R2 − 2R1 = [0,1,−2,1]. Then R1 − R2 = [1,0,3,−1], using the updated second row. These match both displayed steps.

after.name: Question 12
after.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $U$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to each step?

$$
\begin{aligned}[U\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
We write down $U$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $U$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[U\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1},\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2}.
$$

The matrix ${U}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{U}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 12
?

The inverse of the matrix U is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to each step?

[U|I]=[11102301]___________∼[111001−21]___________∼[103−101−21]

a
R2:=R2+(−1)R1,R1:=R1+(−2)R2
b
R2:=R2+2R1,R1:=R1+R2
c
R2:=R2+(−2)R1,R1:=R1+R2
d
R2:=R2+(−2)R1,R1:=R1+(−1)R2
e
R2:=R2+(−3)R1,R1:=R1+(−2)R2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We write down U and the identity matrix I side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix U into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

[U|I]=[11102301]R2:=R2+(−2)R1∼[111001−21]R1:=R1+(−1)R2∼[103−101−21]

The corresponding row operations are R2:=R2+(−2)R1,R1:=R1+(−1)R2.

The matrix U−1 is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore,

U−1=[3−1−21].

content.knowledge_point: Determining the Row Operations Required To Find the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix
content.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $U$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to each step?

$$
\begin{aligned}[U\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
We write down $U$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $U$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[U\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1},\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2}.
$$

The matrix ${U}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{U}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

content.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $A$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to each step?

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -10 & -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 10 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
We write down $A$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $A$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -10 & -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+10{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 10 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+10{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}:=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2}.
$$

The matrix ${A}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{A}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -5 & -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+10{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}:=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2}.
$$

The matrix ${A}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{A}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -5 & -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

\begin{aligned}[V\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2},\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2}.
$$

The matrix ${V}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{V}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

EXPLANATION

content.knowledge_point: Determining the Row Operations Required To Find the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix
content.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $V$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to each step?

$$
\begin{aligned}[V\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
We write down $V$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $V$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[V\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2},\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2}.
$$

The matrix ${V}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{V}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

provenance.kp_title: Determining the Row Operations Required To Find the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix

history.worked_solution:
We write down $V$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $V$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[V\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2},\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2}.
$$

The matrix ${V}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{V}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

[V|I]=[11100201]R2:=12R2∼[111001012]R1:=R1+(−1)R2∼[101−1201012]

The corresponding row operations are R2:=12R2,R1:=R1+(−1)R2.

The matrix V−1 is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore,

V−1=[1−12012].

before.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $Y$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to the blank spaces?

$$
\begin{aligned}[Y\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{3}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

[Y|I]=[2110−1−201]R1:=12R1∼[112120−1−201]R2:=R2+R1∼[1121200−32121]___________∼[11212001−13−23]___________∼[10231301−13−23]

a
R2:=R1+12R2,R1:=−23R2
b
R1:=23R1,R2:=R2+(−12)R1
c

decision.explanation: Multiplying R2 by −2/3 changes [0,−3/2,1/2,1] into [0,1,−1/3,−2/3]. Then subtracting half of the updated R2 from R1 gives [1,0,2/3,1/3]. Both steps match option c.

after.name: Question 15
after.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $Y$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to the blank spaces?

$$
\begin{aligned}[Y\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{3}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
We write down $Y$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $Y$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[Y\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{3}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{2}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}:=-\frac{2}{3}{R}_{2},\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{2}.
$$

The matrix ${Y}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{Y}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}].
$$

EXPLANATION

We write down Y and the identity matrix I side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix Y into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

[Y|I]=[2110−1−201]R1:=12R1∼[112120−1−201]R2:=R2+R1∼[1121200−32121]R2:=−23R2∼[11212001−13−23]R1:=R1+(−12)R2∼[10231301−13−23]

The corresponding row operations are R1:=12R1,R2:=R2+R1,R2:=−23R2,R1:=R1+(−12)R2.

The matrix Y−1 is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore,

Y−1=[2313−13−23].

content.knowledge_point: Determining the Row Operations Required To Find the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix
content.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $Y$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to the blank spaces?

$$
\begin{aligned}[Y\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{3}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
We write down $Y$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $Y$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[Y\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{3}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{2}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}:=-\frac{2}{3}{R}_{2},\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{2}.
$$

The matrix ${Y}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{Y}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}].
$$
